language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Welcome to the first day of diving school! I am your instructor, Naomi. You are in for an exciting adventure under the sea! You will be meeting a lot of different ocean friends today.

Here goes one now! It’s Sam the sea turtle. He is a reptile. How do I know? Well, he is covered in scales and is cold-blooded, that means his body temperature changes with the temperature of his surroundings. And, he was hatched from an egg on land!
As we continue to explore the great deep, can you help me to identify and classify other types of sea creatures and their land-loving friends?

The six main groups of animals are mammals, birds, fish, insects, reptiles, and amphibians. You know that we can sort animals into these groups by identifying characteristics of each. Just like Naomi did with Sam. Come on, let's get to know them a little better!

Welcome to the first day of diving school! I am your instructor, Naomi. You are in for an exciting adventure under the sea! You will be meeting a lot of different ocean friends today.

Here goes one now! It’s Sam the sea turtle. He is a reptile. How do I know? Well, he is covered in scales and is cold-blooded, that means his body temperature changes with the temperature of his surroundings. And, he was hatched from an egg on land!
As we continue to explore the great deep, can you help me to identify and classify other types of sea creatures and their land-loving friends?

The six main groups of animals are mammals, birds, fish, insects, reptiles, and amphibians. You know that we can sort animals into these groups by identifying characteristics of each. Just like Naomi did with Sam. Come on, let's get to know them a little better!

Under water, it is easy to see just how many different types of creatures there are in the world. To help identify and study animals, biologists have come up with ways of sorting animals according to shared characteristics.
I have asked a few animal friends to tell us a bit about themselves. Can you figure out what group they belong to?

When I go scuba diving, I sometimes use my x-ray goggles to see which animals are vertebrates and which animals are invertebrates. Would you like to try them out?
Remember, a vertebrate is an animal with a backbone, and an invertebrate is an animal without a backbone.
